Ratio Scores: 0–100 similarity scores matching the Python `rapidfuzz.fuzz` family. Start with `rapidfuzz_ratio`, or `rapidfuzz_wratio` when you don't know how the strings differ; the `partial_*`, `token_sort_*`, `token_set_*` and `token_*` variants handle fragments, reordered words, and repeated words.
Best Match: Pick the best matches for a string from a list of choices, like Python's `rapidfuzz.process.extract` and `extractOne`, ranked by any ratio or normalized similarity.
Levenshtein: Insertions, deletions and substitutions, each with a configurable cost. Counts characters, unlike DuckDB's built-in byte-based `levenshtein`.
Damerau-Levenshtein: Levenshtein plus swaps of two characters as a single edit, even when other edits happen between them.
Hamming: Position-by-position character match count. Meant for strings of the same length; a shorter input is padded, so each extra character in the longer one counts as a difference.
Indel: Insertion-and-deletion edit distance — no substitutions counted.
Jaro: Jaro similarity — match-and-transposition based. Good for short strings and typos.
Jaro Winkler: Jaro-Winkler — Jaro with extra weight on a shared prefix. Strong default for human names.
Lcs Seq: Longest common subsequence — order-preserving but not adjacency-preserving.
Osa: Optimal String Alignment (a.k.a. restricted Damerau-Levenshtein) — counts adjacent transpositions as a single edit.
Prefix: Edit distance / similarity considering only the matching prefix portion of the strings.
Postfix: Edit distance / similarity considering only the matching suffix portion.
Alignment: Where two strings differ: the edit operations, the equal/changed blocks covering both strings, and where `rapidfuzz_partial_ratio` found its match. Positions are 0-based character offsets.
